summary: The audit checks the first six quarters' coursework (two PHIL 300 proseminars, PHIL 250, three history, two value theory, two language, mind and action, and two metaphysics, epistemology and philosophy of science courses, 49 units in all with other PHIL courses above 110), PHIL 241, two PHIL 301 proseminars, two PHIL seminars numbered 302-399 in the third and fourth years, two quarters of PHIL 500, PHIL 239 twice, and 135 units. Courses for these requirements need a letter grade of B- or better, except Teaching Methods (PHIL 239), the Summer Writer's Workshop (PHIL 241), and the third- and fourth-year seminars, which may be taken credit/no credit. A subplan (Symbolic Systems, History and Philosophy of Science, or Cognitive Science) is optional and adds its own courses. Checked by hand: that the six distribution courses are taken for their maximum units, the second-year writing and oral exam, the chapter oral, colloquium and progress review, three quarters of teaching, candidacy, the defense and the dissertation, plus subplan courses without a list. Symbolic Systems students may skip two of the eight distribution courses, from two different categories; the audit does not apply that, so mark those met by hand.
